result: File passes all checks. Exness median 2.95 pts before the US open (similar to Dukascopy) and 2.93 in US hours (about double Dukascopy's 1.45). The 1.5 assumption is understated.

title: Exness spread by year, 2019-2024
question: Is the Exness spread similar in every year, and are the yearly files usable?

result: Usable: 2021, 2022, 2023 (median 2.75-2.94 pts). Not usable: 2019 and 2020 (too few complete days), 2024 (price gap to HistData 17.29 pts). Exness cannot cover both test periods.

title: Slow multi-market trend (10 markets, monthly) vs benchmarks
question: Does a 12-month trend rule across stocks, energy and currencies earn a positive return after costs, and beat holding the same markets or random directions?
data: FRED daily spot prices and index levels, 10 markets; dev 1988-2010, validation 2011-2024 (2025+ not downloaded)
result: Negative observed result. Net Sharpe +0.32 in 1988-2010 (range -0.07 to +0.71) but -0.30 in 2011-2024. Before costs +0.73 and +0.13: the assumed costs and 2% financing removed the small validation edge. Beat 100% and 94% of random-direction portfolios, and lost far less than always long in its worst months. Amendment 1 (commit 669cbe5) excluded one negative WTI price before any result.

title: Exness cost gate: NAS100 backtest trades re-priced with Exness spread
question: Would the 7 NAS100 strategies still look the same if the 1.5-point backtest spread were replaced by the 2.94-point spread measured on Exness USTEC (p90 stress 3.29/3.65)?
data: backend/data/backtest_trades.csv (bid-only HistData backtest, 4,774 trades 2019-2024); Exness USTEC 2021-2023 spread levels
result: Every strategy got worse: on average 0.109R more cost per trade. All 7 had already failed their main tests, so none is eligible. The only positive split, sweep_mss_fvg 2023-24, fell from +0.150R to +0.100R (stress +0.075R) while its 2019-22 split is -0.238R. The gate is now a permanent extra rule before anything can be added to scanner.QUALIFIED.

title: Turn of the month: hold the Nasdaq over each month end (own idea)
question: Does holding the Nasdaq Composite from the second-to-last trading day of a month to the 3rd trading day of the next earn more than random timing, after Exness-like spread and overnight financing?
data: FRED NASDAQCOM daily closes; dev 1971-1999, validation 2000-2024 (2025+ locked)
result: Inconclusive, the best result so far but not a pass. 1971-1999 passed every check (+0.50% per trade after costs, range +0.23% to +0.74%, beat 100% of random timing). 2000-2024 stayed positive (+0.19% per trade, stress +0.06%) but the range crossed zero (-0.13% to +0.52%) and it beat only 86% of random timing (95% required). The effect looks smaller since it became famous.

title: News effect: how much NAS100, gold and BTC move in the 30 minutes after each US high-impact release
question: How many times bigger is the 30-minute range after CPI, NFP, FOMC, GDP and PCE than at the same time on nearby days without news, per market?
data: HistData NSXUSD and XAUUSD, Binance BTCUSDT M1, events 2019-2024 (2025+ locked)
result: News makes the first 30 minutes much bigger than normal: NAS100 CPI 3.3x, NFP 3.5x, FOMC 2.9x; gold FOMC 6.1x, CPI 2.8x, NFP 2.9x; BTC 1.9-2.4x for CPI/NFP/FOMC; GDP and PCE 1.2-1.8x. Size only: the measure says nothing about direction. Shown on the dashboard News card and in the Telegram heads-up 30 minutes before each release; the +-30-minute blackout is unchanged.

result: Running automatically (app/core/tom_forward.py, dashboard Results card, Telegram). No verdict before 36 trades (about 3 years). First 2 trades: +2.33% and -3.46% after costs. Paper only; never ordered.

title: Buy the drop: Nasdaq at a 10-day-low close, hold 5 days (the one unfreeze idea)
question: Does buying the Nasdaq Composite at a close that is the lowest of the last 10 trading days and selling 5 trading days later earn more than random timing, after Exness-like spread and overnight financing, in both 1971-1999 and 2000-2024?
data: FRED NASDAQCOM daily closes; dev 1971-1999, validation 2000-2024 (2025+ locked)
result: Negative observed result. 1971-1999: 446 trades, -0.342% per trade after costs (-0.184% before costs), range -0.626% to -0.030%, beat 0% of random timing, 7 of 29 years positive, 0 of 4 nearby settings positive. 2000-2024: 400 trades, +0.203% (stress +0.045%) but the range crosses zero (-0.122% to +0.526%) and it beat only 87% of random timing. Before 2000 Nasdaq daily moves tended to continue (autocorrelation +0.205), so drops kept going. Project re-frozen (CLAUDE.md 2a).
